title: Share courses with participants → Learner Portal
intro: Semester → Courses → Share with participants → Learner Portal. Evidence for moving a course from setup to learner access, and making the first visit useful. Group assignment belongs to 04; reports to 08; announcements and material delivery to 09. Screens are research captures, not verification of current product capabilities.

questions.title: Publish model (single toggle vs. per-item visibility vs. scheduled release)
questions.answer: Publication is layered in these captures. Teachable [mobbin:9ef7d498-63b5-4d12-a94f-5779c906f717] shows lesson Publish controls and a Drip panel based on days after enrolment. Kajabi [mobbin:9aa981d2-b178-4843-b8dd-0685815ecd62] shows Draft, Publish, Drip and Lock in a module menu, followed by a Published state. Podia [mobbin:94f6be70-d9b2-4363-8091-62d20f8d1f9e] separates Published, Open and Visible and shows a delayed module. Circle [mobbin:ec16c800-3b82-4f66-8b88-76840a7590dc] explains Open, Private and Secret audiences. For Essentials, make course publication, audience scope and item release separately legible. The captures do not establish the consequences of unpublishing an active course.

questions.title: Access grant paths (enrolled groups / link / code / email) and how permission levels are expressed
questions.answer: Grant access in the context of the course. Circle [mobbin:e801d8ae-1e7e-45e3-9035-0452816271e5] shows invitations with selected-space access and privileged-role controls. Figma [mobbin:b227715d-bc5d-4655-9133-921c156f6837] combines email invitations, copy link and visible permissions; Figma [mobbin:ffaf7085-3f32-450d-938b-812274011f53] adds Anyone access, View/Edit and password protection. Notion [mobbin:44650693-5283-421a-b978-d4cf1a8de987] names a Member role in an email invitation. These are access patterns, not a prescribed role model for learners. A password is not evidence of a classroom join-code workflow; enrolled-group inheritance and class codes remain unverified in this set. Podia [mobbin:157502c1-8bd1-4fd3-aae9-97358b725cad] makes a 30-day trial limit explicit before inviting a customer. Gumroad [refero:11b3c0a4-eb09-4d98-9a1a-742439189540] is a creator-side counter-example: Share and Collaborators navigation do not establish a learner-access workflow.

questions.title: "Preview as learner" availability and fidelity
questions.answer: Preview has different scopes. Circle [mobbin:02f1cfb0-ef6b-4f9f-8218-bfe24c660981] explicitly labels preview as an enrolled member and retains lesson content and a completion action. Canva [mobbin:5c96453b-0c58-434f-94ba-c6d68a8f5bd5] places View as learner beside the course editor. Teachable [mobbin:e6757446-af84-43d5-bed0-da79c9a3826c] exposes curriculum preview without proving the same role simulation. SchoolAI [mobbin:56f720b3-daec-4967-9fc4-60a7f8501c55] previews an AI activity as a student, which is narrower than a whole course portal. For Essentials, label the simulated learner and group; confirm separately whether release dates, prerequisites and progress writes are simulated. Those behaviours are not established by the screenshots.

questions.title: Learner course home: what is above the fold (next session, progress, materials, announcements)
questions.answer: Day one needs a clear next action. Teachable [mobbin:c04c0023-2365-4741-9dc9-4592f491c7ea] shows Start Lesson, the lesson list and 0% completion. Coursera [mobbin:18683325-d982-4756-b06e-4ed52c933b06] prioritises Continue learning, progress, Resume and a weekly goal. Circle [mobbin:afde5712-b2c0-4fc1-be7b-4ac42446d642] provides community context and content entry points. For simulation education, adapt the next-action pattern to the next scheduled session and required preparation; these captures do not establish a session-first portal. Treat announcements as context from module 09 and recordings/reports as a hand-off to 08.

questions.title: Feedback to instructor that sharing worked (who has opened, pending invites)
questions.answer: Publishing, inviting, joining and learning are different events. Podia [mobbin:6462b667-d688-4634-a413-c914bdc3b20a] shows Customer invited alongside audience rows and progress; this supports an action confirmation and participation context, not email-open telemetry. Slack [mobbin:2fe9271e-36ed-4333-b809-6078dc790098] exposes Pending and Accepted tabs plus bounced, resent and revoked invitation states. Pending does not prove delivery. For Essentials, show the recipient, current access and available recovery action, then distinguish invitation status from first course access and learning progress. No retained capture demonstrates a course-open event. Canva [mobbin:a906866c-f694-41fd-b437-b086430c1585] confirms the course is ready, reports team notification and offers Classwork and Copy link; it does not enumerate learner acceptance.

questions.title: Cross-device (web vs. mobile portal) parity
questions.answer: Only Coursera has a matched web/iOS course-home pair in this set: Coursera [mobbin:f31fedca-3104-45d9-a48e-08afa231c723] and Coursera [mobbin:d76cce29-fa86-4e42-a549-54d3765ad5d9]. Both expose progress and the next learning action; goals and navigation adapt to the device. The iOS Download button shows an available action, not verified offline behaviour. Udemy [mobbin:89b6481f-0676-46bb-a15b-daa62b8a10cd] is Udemy mobile context without a matched web capture; Teachable [mobbin:be865fb9-7894-4e03-8262-c14a16d810e3] is a Teachable learner-facing preview inside an admin shell, not a verified ordinary learner session; no matched mobile capture was retained. Preserve shared learner state and the next action across devices, but validate invitation entry, authentication and session joining separately.

references.title: Publishing a course space
references.question: Q1
references.take: Circle’s publishing flow exposes draft mode and Open/Private/Secret audience descriptions, then topics, thumbnail and Save changes; Open refers to community members, not the public internet.

references.title: Publishing course content
references.question: Q1
references.take: Kajabi’s module menu offers Draft, Publish, Drip and Lock; choosing Publish produces a Published state and confirmation toast.

references.title: Publishing a course
references.question: Q1
references.take: Podia confirms Course published, separates Published/Open/Visible, and shows a delayed module plus an audience table with progress, signup, start and expiry columns.

references.title: Course publish settings
references.question: Q1
references.take: Teachable places per-lesson Publish actions beside a Drip panel with days after enrolment, Activate drip, notification controls and saved feedback.

references.title: Course visibility state
references.question: Q1
references.take: Teachable’s curriculum combines Preview and per-lesson Publish controls with a Drip panel that visibly requires a plan upgrade.

references.title: Course release control
references.question: Q1
references.take: Teachable’s Drip panel exposes days after enrolment, a numeric delay, Activate drip, student notification controls and saved feedback.

references.title: Community access dialog
references.question: Q2
references.take: Circle’s Invite members screen combines selected-space access with admin/moderator permission controls and Send invites; privilege assignment is separate from choosing spaces.

references.title: Invite and permission dialog
references.question: Q2
references.take: Figma combines email invitation, Copy link, existing people and can-view permissions in one dialog; this is a content-sharing analogy for course access.

references.title: Link sharing permission state
references.question: Q2
references.take: Figma exposes Anyone access, View/Edit, optional password protection and a viewers-can-copy/save/export setting before Save; a password is not a classroom join code.

references.title: Digital course content manager
references.question: Q2
references.take: Counter-example in scope: Gumroad’s creator content editor has a Share tab and Collaborators navigation, but this capture does not show a learner-access grant or invitation status.

references.title: Page sharing dialog
references.question: Q2
references.take: Notion’s Add members modal supports names or emails, an explained Member role, an invitation message and Send invite; workspace membership is an adjacent analogy, not course enrolment.

references.title: Guest access state
references.question: Q2
references.take: Notion shows a typed email suggestion labelled Guest alongside Member role selection, an invite message and Send invite; inspect identity and role labels together.

references.title: Invite a customer modal
references.question: Q2
references.take: Podia’s Invite a customer modal captures email entry, optional tags, a time-limited access warning, and explicit Don’t invite/Invite customer actions; targeted enrolment evidence, but no role selector or access code/link is visible.

references.title: View as learner flow
references.question: Q3
references.take: Captured two-step flow explicitly names View as learner and shows the resulting learner-facing state, strong evidence for a low-friction preview entry and fidelity check.

references.title: Preview lesson flow
references.question: Q3
references.take: Captured six-step lesson preview flow shows preview can preserve real lesson navigation and content context; use as evidence for fidelity, with learner role labeling kept visible.

references.title: AI classroom learner view (preview analogy)
references.question: Q3
references.take: Counter-example in scope: “Previewing as a student” and Restart preview are visible for an AI activity; this does not establish whole-course or cohort-access preview.

references.title: Curriculum preview flow
references.question: Q3
references.take: Counter-example in scope: Curriculum Preview is visible in the author setup flow; the retained steps do not establish the explicit enrolled-member simulation shown by Circle.

references.title: Community space home (learner home analogy)
references.question: Q4
references.take: Captured community home is an adjacent course-home analogy: orient the learner with a clear space title and content entry points above the fold; course progress and next session were not observed.

references.title: Course community home with content feed
references.question: Q4
references.take: Captured home puts the community/course identity and latest content in the first view; use this as an adjacent learner-home pattern, with progress and next session needing explicit slots.

references.title: Learner course home
references.question: Q4
references.take: Coursera foregrounds Continue learning, course progress, a module card, Resume and a weekly goal; session scheduling and announcements are not observed here.

references.title: Learner course dashboard
references.question: Q4
references.take: Teachable’s learner home shows Start Lesson, a lesson list and 0% completion, giving the new learner a clear first action.

references.title: Course ready sharing confirmation
references.question: Q5
references.take: Canva’s post-publish confirmation says Your course is ready, notes team notification, and offers Go to Classwork plus Copy link; strong feedback that sharing/publishing succeeded, without pending/accepted learner counts.

references.title: Invite customer to course
references.question: Q5
references.take: Podia’s captured invitation flow shows Customer invited, audience rows with progress, and Customers/Pending analytics; these states do not establish email delivery, acceptance or course opening.

references.title: Workspace invite confirmation
references.question: Q5
references.take: Slack’s invitation management shows Requests/Pending/Accepted/Invite Links tabs plus bounced, resent and revoked invitation states, providing recovery evidence beyond a success message.

references.title: Course dashboard web
references.question: Q6
references.take: Coursera’s web home shows enrolled learning, progress, Resume and a weekly goal; pair with its iOS reference to compare the core learner hierarchy.

references.title: Course dashboard mobile
references.question: Q6
references.take: Coursera iOS shows module progress, Download, daily goals and Up Next; its matched web capture supports hierarchy parity, not verified offline or invite behaviour.

references.title: Course learner portal
references.question: Q6
references.take: Teachable shows a learner-facing home inside an Edit in Admin / Preview as admin shell, with Draft lesson states, Start actions and 0% completion; this is preview context, not a verified ordinary learner session.

references.title: Course dashboard mobile
references.question: Q6
references.take: Udemy’s iOS learner course home provides mobile context; no matched web capture was retained, so cross-device parity remains unverified.
